For every ordered derivative of length at most $N$, assume the initial value divided by $g(l)$ is bounded by $B$, the forcing divided by $g(t)$ by $H$, and every positive-order coefficient derivative by $C$, uniformly on $S$. Here $K,B,H,C\ge0$. Then on $[l,r]\times S$ each solution derivative satisfies $\|\partial^w x(t,p)\|/g(t)\le\Phi_N(K(r-l)C)K(B+(r-l)H)$. The universal factor is nonnegative and nondecreasing in its argument. No smallness of $C$ is assumed.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_pressu: Fix $N\in\mathbb N$ and nonnegative constants $W_j$. Assume Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2 and the weighted derivative recurrence supplied by Lemma D.3. Let $\mathsf D,\mathsf D_0\ge1$, $\mathsf D_0^{64}\le\mathsf D$, $\ell_*>0$ and $\ell_*\mathsf D^{16}\le1$. Each coefficient $c=M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2$ must be smooth on $\mathbb R^3$ and satisfy $\|D^jc(a)\|\le W_j\mathsf D_0^{16(j+1)}$ for every $j,a$. There is $C\ge1$, fixed before these coefficients and scales, such that every derivative of order $0\le j\le N$ of the three rescaled coefficients $c(\ell_*a)$ is bounded respectively by $C\mathsf D$, $C\mathsf D^2$ and $C\mathsf D^4$. These are operator-norm bounds, uniform in $a$. The statement assumes neither $\lambda\ne0$ nor $\kappa\ne0$; division by zero is zero. Source and velocity estimates are still needed for (5.24).
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.transverseCofra: Assume Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2 and the weighted derivative recurrence supplied by Lemma D.3. Let $\mathsf D\ge1$, $W_j\ge0$, $\kappa(a)=G(a)^Tk$ and $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$. Suppose $F,G,M,P_\kappa$ are smooth matrix fields on $\mathbb R^3$, each satisfying $\|D^jc(a)\|\le W_j\mathsf D^{16(j+1)}$. Then $G(I-P_\kappa)$ and $-2G(I-P_\kappa)MF$ satisfy the respective bounds $C_j\mathsf D^{32(j+1)}$ and $C'_j\mathsf D^{64(j+1)}$ for every derivative order, with constants fixed before $k,\mathsf D,F,G,M$. The product estimate of Lemma D.2 proves these bounds. No inverse relation between $F,G$ is required. For the parent deformation they encode the projected inverse and the right-hand-side coefficient in (5.18). At $\kappa=0$, division by zero makes $P_\kappa=0$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.IsExpansion.ina: The profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$ and obey the phase period and coupled label translations; $0<2\ell_*<1/2$ keeps the envelope inside each cell. For any expansion satisfying the recurrence, $V_p$, $\mathsf p_p$, the curl corrections through $C_{P+1}$, and the transverse sources vanish before $t_0$ and outside the envelope. The envelope must fit strictly inside the label cell. These are the support conclusions of Proposition 5.4; the mean fields are not required to vanish before activation.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.main_towe: Assume smooth periodic $v=z_t$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$, an endpoint inverse of norm at most $A$, and the explicit small bounds on positive-order coefficient derivatives. Applying Lemma D.3 to the integrated mean equation (4.9) gives higher-order Hölder estimates for $v=z_t$. Differentiation preserves divergence freedom and both zero displacement endpoints. The coefficient bound distinguishes multiplication by $K$ from time integration of $\Omega$, whose contribution has the additional factor $T$. This is the analytic lifting step behind (5.14).
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_A_bound: Assume $\mathsf D\ge2$ and nonnegative supplied upper bounds for the zeroth and first coefficient quantities. The inverse exponent and its prefactor are fixed in advance. Polynomial bounds for the zeroth and first derivatives of $K$ and $\Omega$ place the expression in (4.10) below one power $\mathsf D^{C_A}$. This is an arithmetic estimate once those coefficient bounds are supplied. The proof of (5.14) provides their analytic interpretation and uses the resulting exponent to choose the radius threshold in (5.13).
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_KOmega_p: Assume Proposition 5.1 and Lemma D.2 for a smooth periodic solenoidal parent on $[0,T]$ with the band, deformation, residual and coercivity bounds of §5.1. Proposition 5.1 and the product rule of Lemma D.2 give polynomial derivative bounds for $K=(D_aX)^TD_aX$ and $\Omega=(D_aX)^T(M^T-M)D_aX$. Their constants are chosen uniformly before the parent. Low orders bound the endpoint inverse constant, while positive orders become small after multiplication by the radius weights in (5.13).
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_velocity: The domain is $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$; spatial derivatives are taken on its periodic lift and measured in operator norm. Bernstein's inequality bounds the positive-order derivatives of a smooth periodic velocity using its gradient bound. The estimate allows Fourier support up to $4\mathsf D$ and $\mathsf D\ge1$, whereas Proposition 5.1 uses $2\mathsf D$ and $\mathsf D\ge2$. No estimate of the undifferentiated velocity is needed for this step of the parent coefficient argument.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leadingSwitch: Assume a seed solving the transverse homogeneous equation, a smooth time cutoff and an expansion whose first profiles equal the cutoff times that seed wave and its pressure. The switched leading wave satisfies $V_{1,t}+MV_1+\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_1=\widetilde\chi^{\prime}A_1$. This follows by differentiating the cutoff times the homogeneous leading solution, including times before activation. It is the first identity in the proof of Proposition 5.4; the activation contribution of the curl correction is added separately in the full residual.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.lemma55_main: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, a smooth odd periodic solenoidal parent with the band, deformation, residual and coercivity bounds, and a nonzero stable central seed with positive coupling and $0<\gamma\le1$. Proposition 5.1 and the product, derivative, and phase primitive estimates of Lemma D.1 give both bounds in Lemma 5.5. The parent exponent is independent of derivative order. The formal hypotheses require zero phase averages of the velocity and source on the whole interval, with transversality and the momentum equation imposed on the active interval.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSolvable_of: The source is smooth, periodic and phase independent; the displacement is required to vanish at both $0$ and $T$, not its velocity. Theorem 4.2 supplies the smooth mean solution required by the recursion under the parent hypotheses of §5.1. The integrated transported forcing determines the displacement velocity, from which $B$ and its normalized pressure are recovered. This establishes existence for (5.11); the separate uniqueness argument identifies any other admissible mean solution with it.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, the parent coefficient, residual and coercivity bounds, and a nonzero central transverse seed with relative forward growth at most $\mathsf D$ and coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$. Proposition 5.1 allows one sufficiently small envelope on which every seed with initial data (5.4) satisfies the quantitative near-origin estimates. Uniqueness identifies that seed with the separately constructed local solution. The conclusion includes more than (5.19), but its relative-error constant is only specified as a function of $\mathsf D$; this statement does not expose a polynomial bound for that constant.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence: Here $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*\ne0$, the parent is smooth, periodic and volume preserving, and all constraints hold throughout $[0,T]$. A zero-mean transverse profile satisfies $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot(V+C[V])=0$. The proof uses the identity $V+C[V]=\widetilde{\mathbf d}\times Q[V]$ in the transported parent geometry. Proposition 5.4 sums these completed oscillations and the separately divergence-free means to obtain the divergence constraint for the entire finite correction.

The parent is smooth and volume preserving on $[0,T]$, and the smooth periodic displacement satisfies $z(0)=z(T)=0$. The endpoint mean solution has $B=D_aXz_t$ with divergence-free label velocity $z_t$. Volume preservation and the Piola identity give $\mathbf d\cdot B=0$, and phase independence makes this the full divergence constraint as well. This supplies the mean terms in the divergence calculation for $W$ in Proposition 5.4.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.HigherHessianCl: Fix sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, and a finite expansion of depth $P\ge2$ over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$. The hypotheses include Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. The central pair has activation frequency $\lambda\ge1$, positive transverse stability as in (5.5), and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Under $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the assertion is $\|D_x^2\sum_{p=2}^{P}\mathsf p_p^\natural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$ on $[0,T]$. The exponent and constants precede the parent and expansion. This declaration states the intermediate claim; the accompanying theorem proves it. No zero-mean Poisson requirement is imposed on the parent pressure.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.MeanHessianClai: For a finite expansion of depth $P\ge2$, take a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Require a nonzero transverse central seed of activation frequency $\lambda\ge1$, the stability and coupling conditions (5.5), and $0<\gamma\le1$. With sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the assertion is $\|D_x^2\sum_{p=2}^{P}\bar q_p^\natural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2}$ throughout $[0,T]$. It concerns the mean pressures belonging to that expansion. Constants are chosen before the parent and profiles. This declaration formulates the claim; it does not itself supply its proof.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl: Assume the phase-profile normalization, existence and uniqueness of the finite expansion, its level estimates, and the physical derivative bounds of Lemma 5.7. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over a smooth periodic odd divergence-free parent satisfying the deformation, residual and coercivity bounds of §5.1, take a nonzero stable transverse seed with $0<\gamma\le1$ and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$. Once the envelope is sufficiently small and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ satisfies $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the conclusion is $\|D V(t,0)-D U(t,0)-\widetilde\chi(t)\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes\kappa(t,0)\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ for $t\in[t_0,T]$. The proof first bounds the higher-gradient error by $K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$ and then absorbs $\lambda^{-1/12}$. Constants precede the parent and expansion; the theorem is conditional on the listed earlier mathematical results.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_cutoffBo: Let $V,R_V$ be jointly smooth periodic fields on $[0,T]$, with $V$ divergence free, and let $\Pi(t,\cdot)$ be smooth and periodic at each time. Assume $V_t+V\cdot\nabla V+\nabla\Pi=R_V$. For $P\ge2$, $\Lambda\ge1$ and a smooth radial cutoff $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on the unit ball and zero outside radius two, take an already constructed stage $u=S_\Lambda V,p$. Given the real and complex Fourier tail estimates and Hölder product bound, constants independent of $T,\Lambda,V$ give $\|u(t)-V(t)\|_{C^{2,1/2}}\le K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$. Separately, each of $\|R_u(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}$ and $\|D^2(p-\Pi)(t)\|_{C^{0,1/2}}$ is at most $C\|R_V(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$, where $\varepsilon_\Lambda=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$. These are pointwise-in-time estimates; the summed bound in (5.56) follows after enlarging constants. No time regularity of $\Pi$ is assumed.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.higherHessianCl: Assume the parent coefficient estimates, existence of the finite expansion, the hierarchy bounds, the physical derivative estimates and the finite-norm product estimates. For $P\ge2$, $0<T\le1$ and a smooth periodic parent satisfying the deformation, Fourier, residual and coercivity assumptions of §5.1, the formal statement proves $\|D_x^2\sum_{p=2}^{P}\mathsf p_p^\natural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$ on $[0,T]$, under the central stability and coupling hypotheses, $0<\gamma\le1$ and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. Constants precede the parent and expansion. The proof uses $\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_p=P_\kappa(f_p+f_p^S-2MV_p)$ before taking one more physical derivative. Taking two unrestricted physical derivatives would instead leave $\lambda^{1/12}$. This proves the intermediate assertion (5.52), conditional on the stated earlier estimates.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leadingHessianC: Assume the phase-profile bounds, parent coefficient estimates, localized seed bounds, hierarchy estimates and finite-norm product estimates. For a finite expansion over a smooth periodic parent satisfying §5.1, with $\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma\le1$, sufficiently small envelope and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the leading pressure satisfies $D_x^2\mathsf p_1^\natural\le K\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$. The coefficient $c_{\mathbf a}=2\widetilde\chi g(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$ is nonnegative, and the lower bound on $F_h\,{}^{\prime}$ controls $-c_{\mathbf a}F_h\,{}^{\prime}\kappa\otimes\kappa$ from above. The remaining tensors are bounded in norm. The formal proof obtains the leading pressure norm from the hierarchy estimate at level one; the paper cites (5.22). This difference concerns the argument, not the signed conclusion.

For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over the smooth periodic parent of §5.1, with its stable positively coupled nonzero seed, $0<\gamma\le1$ and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the formal statement proves $\|D_x^2\sum_{p=2}^{P} ar q_p^
atural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2}$ throughout $[0,T]$. The exponent and constants precede the parent and expansion. The mean equations give $\Delta ar q^
atural=\operatorname{div} ar f^
atural-2\operatorname{tr}(

notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.truncatedParent: Let $P\ge2$, $\Lambda\ge1$, and let the periodic fields satisfy $V\in C^{P,1/2}$ and $R_V\in C^{1,1/2}$. Assume the real and complex Fourier tail estimates, a Hölder product estimate, a bounded linear projection on $C^{1,1/2}$, and the specified bounded bilinear product and contraction. Put $u=S_\Lambda V$ and $\varepsilon_\Lambda=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}})^2$. Then $u-V\in C^{2,1/2}$ and the projected expression in (5.58) belongs to $C^{1,1/2}$, with bounds $K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$ and $C\|R_V\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$. The constant may depend on those operators, but not on the fields or cutoff frequency. This is a spatial estimate for an algebraically defined expression; its identification with the physical residual uses a separate momentum identity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve: Assume a common sequence with the smoothness, frequency schedule, residual, support and increment bounds of Theorem 7.1, and a smooth Euler limit $u$ with the earlier-interval convergence of Proposition 8.1. Then there is a continuous $w$ on $[0,T_\infty]\times\mathbb R^3$ such that $U_j\to w$ uniformly there and $u(t)=w(t)$ for $0\le t<T_\infty$. Periodicity of the approximations identifies this with the closed torus slab. The proof uses $\|U_j-U_{j-1}\|_\infty\le2\lambda_j^{-1}$ and summability of the reciprocal frequencies. Unlike the declaration that merely selects the Section 8 construction, this result includes the closed-interval limit. It asserts continuity at the origin at the terminal time, not spatial smoothness there.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveOrig: For every real $\rho$, every $T\ge0$ and every $\lambda>0$, the formal theorem constructs nonzero perpendicular paths $\kappa,\mathbf a$ solving the central wave equations over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ on $[0,T]$. They start with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$ and $\mathbf a(0)=c e_2$, $c>0$, and attain $\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|=\lambda^{-3/4}$. The proof verifies explicit paths and rescales their positive maximum. The mathematical existence conclusion agrees with the other first-wave existence theorem; using explicit formulas is a difference of proof, not of statement. No short-interval condition is needed for existence, and $T=0$ is permitted.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.first_couplin: Assume the frame identities of Lemma 2.2. Let the first central wave over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ start with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$ and amplitude in the positive $e_2$ direction, and remain nonzero and transverse on $[0,T]$. If $\lambda>0$, $|\rho|\le1$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, then $E_1(t)\cdot B_\rho E_2(t)\ge\pi$ for every $t\in[0,T]$. The proof obtains $|E_1'|,|E_2'|\le\|B_\rho\|$ and a coupling variation of at most $2t\|B_\rho\|^2$. Only the final positivity bound is stated as the conclusion. The formal assumption on $\rho$ allows negative values and zero as well as the paper's range.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.proposition82: Assume Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.4 and B.1, a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, and its smooth odd Euler limit $u$ from Proposition 8.1. Then $\sup_{0\le t<T_\infty}\|u(t)\|_\infty<\infty$ and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$. More precisely, there are fixed real $c>0,C$ such that, for every sufficiently large $j$ and every $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$. The constants precede the choice of $j$ and $t$. This estimate concerns the limiting solution, whereas (8.2) concerns $U_j$ and retains $\lambda_{j-2}^9$. The extra conclusion is used with crossing-time bounds to prove integral divergence. The supremum norm is the essential supremum over one spatial period.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_sub_sqrt_o: Let $v:\mathbb R^3\to X$ be differentiable, where $X$ is a real normed space. Suppose $A,B\ge0$, $|v(x)|\le A$, and $\|Dv(x)\|\le B$ for every $x$, with the operator norm on the derivative. The formal statement proves $|v(x)-v(y)|\le\sqrt{2AB}\,|x-y|^{1/2}$ for all $x,y$. It combines the bounds $2A$ and $B|x-y|$ and yields the interpolation inequality preceding (D.2). The domain here is all of $\mathbb R^3$; periodicity and a time variable are unnecessary. The hypotheses are actual pointwise bounds, so no unproved supremum finiteness is implicit.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.MeanParentFlow: The setting is $0<T\le1$ and a velocity $u$ smooth on the closed slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, periodic under integer translations and divergence free. A supplied family $X_{s,t}$ is the particle flow of $u$. The paper's map is $X(t,a)=X_{0,t}(a)$, while $X_{t,0}$ is the reverse map. Thus the domain is $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, represented by periodic lifts. This precisely records the standing setting of §4; no Euler equation or bound on $H^\#$ is included here.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.ModelCase: For the preceding wave’s moving frame and its positive activation couplings $\nu=B_{12}(t_0)$ and $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)$, the formal condition requires $B_{12}(t_0+\tau/r)=\nu$, $B_{32}(t_0+\tau/r)=\eta$, all other frame entries zero, and $E_c(t_0+\tau/r)=0$ for every $0\le\tau\le T$. These are the model assumptions of Lemma 2.3, in a frame that may itself rotate. The condition does not mean that $B$ is constant in fixed spatial coordinates. It neither constructs a new wave nor asserts that the physical interval lies in the compact set where the preceding wave equations are assumed; both are separate hypotheses.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.NewWaveVector: The formal condition requires $\lambda>0$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$ and $k'=-M^Tk$ throughout the compact physical time set $I$, where $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$ and $E_3$ is the preceding wave’s third unit direction. Derivatives are taken relative to $I$. This matches the wave-vector data in §2.2.1. No amplitude or amplitude initial value is specified. The path $k$ is formally defined for all real times, but the equation is required only on $I$; the amplification theorems separately require $[t_0,t_0+T/r]\subseteq I$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.ProfileFamily: This condition on two real families $F_h,P_h$ states all properties in Lemma 3.1. For $0<h\le1$, $F_h$ is smooth, odd and period one, while $P_h$ is smooth, period one, has mean zero over $[0,1]$, and satisfies $P_h'=F_h$. A single positive $C$, independent of $h$ and phase, gives $F_h'(0)=1$, $-Ch\le F_h'\le1$ and $|F_h|\le Ch$. For each integer $j\ge2$, a positive $C_j$ independent of $h,s$ gives $|\partial_s^jF_h|\le C_jh^{1-j}$. The exponent is an integer, so it is negative when $j\ge2$. Pointwise phase bounds encode the supremum bounds. This condition does not itself assert that such a family exists.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_13_of: Assuming Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.2 and the half-Hölder comparison (D.2), the formal implication proves (5.13). For the smooth periodic parent, let $K=DX^TDX$, $\Omega=DX^T(M^T-M)DX$ and $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$. At sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, every $m\ge1$ satisfies $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$, with finite norms on $[0,T]$. The threshold depends on $C_A$, not on the derivative order. The implication does not itself identify $A$ with an endpoint inverse bound.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_14_of: Assuming Theorem 4.2, Proposition 5.1, Lemmas D.2–D.3 and (5.13), the formal implication proves the mean estimate (5.14). For a smooth periodic mean solution on $[0,T]$, write $B=DXv$, $v=z_t$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}_av=0$ and $g=DX^T\bar f$. A finite scaled half-Hölder norm of $g$ gives $\|v\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|g\|_{[n],1/2}$ and a finite output norm. The radius is fixed sufficiently small before the parent and order. Multiplication by $K$ and time integration of $\Omega v$ are treated separately; the latter contributes a factor $T\le1$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_59: For an integer $m\ge0$, let $f:\mathbb R^3\to E$ and $g:\mathbb R^3\to F$ have finite $C^{m,1/2}$ norms, where $E,F,G$ are real normed spaces. If $B:E\times F\to G$ is continuous and bilinear, then $x\mapsto B(f(x),g(x))$ belongs to $C^{m,1/2}$ and its norm is at most $3(m+1)2^m\|B\|\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$. This proves (5.59) for scalar and tensor products and also covers other bilinear operations. The factor $\|B\|$ is necessary when the operation is rescaled. Periodicity is not required for this estimate on $\mathbb R^3$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_D_2: Let $0<\ell_*\le1$ and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, where $X$ is any real normed space. Assume all derivatives through order $n+1$ are uniformly bounded in time and label. The formal statement proves $\|c\|_{[n]}\le\|c\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|c\|_{[n+1]}$ and establishes finiteness of the Hölder quantities. At each order $m$ it also proves $\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}(\ell_*^m|c|_m+\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1})$. Each multi-index is counted once. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; their sum is equivalent within a factor two. Thus the explicit constant four yields the paper's unspecified constant after the chosen norm convention is accounted for.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.section8_set: Assuming Theorem 7.1, the formal statement selects admissible parameters, an inductive construction, a strength constant and a finite positive time $T_\infty$. The construction has the smooth periodic approximate velocities, residual and central-wave estimates, shrinking supports, summable increments and activation times converging to $T_\infty$ required by that theorem. Every stage is defined beyond this common time. The conclusion establishes the existence of this setting; it contains neither a velocity $w$ nor a convergence assertion. Thus it supports the opening choice in Section 8, while the next claim, uniform convergence on the closed terminal interval, needs a separate theorem.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.corollary_8_3: Assume the common construction of Theorem 7.1, its smooth odd Euler limit $u,p$ from Proposition 8.1, and the formal conclusions of Proposition 8.2. These include fixed $c>0,C$ with $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late interval $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. Then $u$ is maximal at $T_\infty>0$, every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same data has that lifespan, and both integrals in (1.2) are infinite. The proof combines the displayed lower bound with lower bounds for the crossing durations. It does not infer integral divergence from pointwise blow-up alone. The paper instead invokes the periodic Beale–Kato–Majda criterion; the formal proof establishes this construction-specific conclusion without proving that general criterion.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_1_3: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, and $\mathcal B(s)>0$ satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$. Suppose $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. Then $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for $j\ge1$. Thus the last expression is exactly (1.15), since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$. The formal statement omits threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination from §1.5; the arithmetic result therefore applies under fewer assumptions.

u,\eta$. Set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/

All profiles have phase period one and the label translation law needed for periodic physical evaluation. This defines the requirements; it does not prove existence or estimates.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed: Let $M(t,a)=\nabla U(t,X_{0,t}(a))$ and $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. A seed is a smooth field $\mathbf a$ on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ which agrees with the central seed at $a=0$, starts from $(I-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})\mathbf a(t_0,0)$, and solves $\partial_t\mathbf a=-M\mathbf a+2\kappa(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$ while satisfying $\kappa\cdot\mathbf a=0$. The differential equation uses derivatives within $[t_0,T]$ at its endpoints. This records the seed equation and (5.4), not the amplitude and coupling estimates on nearby labels. Those are later conclusions. Nonvanishing of $\kappa$ comes from the parent flow and nonzero carrier, not from this declaration alone.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation: This condition identifies $u$ with $S_\Lambda V$ on $[0,T]$ by requiring the cutoff formula for every continuous function on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ representing $V$. At each time, $p$ must be smooth, periodic, have zero integral over the centered unit cell, and solve $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Existence of a continuous periodic representative of $V$ is not included in this condition: without one, its cutoff clause alone imposes no restriction. Proposition 5.11 supplies such a representative by proving $V$ smooth and periodic. The condition specifies the pressure spatially at each time; joint time smoothness is proved for the constructed truncation.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Launch: The conditions are $0\le t_0<T$, $k_*\ne0$, and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, with $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. They specify the activation time and the frequency convention in §5.1. Thus $\lambda$ is the length of the transported vector at the origin when the wave is activated, not automatically $|k_*|$. These conditions do not themselves assert that $X$ is a differentiable flow or that $\lambda\ge1$; those requirements are supplied by the parent hypotheses. Together with the bounds for the forward and inverse deformation, they give (5.3).
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution: On $[0,T]$, let $X$ be the parent flow, $M=DU\circ X$ and $\mathbf d=(D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a$. The formal condition on smooth phase-independent $B,\bar q$ is $B_t+MB+\mathbf d\bar q=\bar f$, with smooth periodic fields $z,v$ satisfying $z_t=v$, $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $B=D_aXv$. Volume preservation converts this to $\mathbf d\cdot B=0$, as in (5.11). The pressure’s spatial mean is not fixed here. The conditions select $B(0)$ through both displacement endpoints; they do not require zero initial velocity or vanishing before activation.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin: On $[t_0,T]$, the central seed $\mathbf a(t,0)$ and $\kappa(t,0)$ are nonzero and perpendicular, solve their coupled linear transport equations, and satisfy both conditions (5.5): every transverse solution grows relative to the seed by at most $\mathsf D$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. The formal normalization is only $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. With $\lambda\ge1$ from the parent, $\gamma$ is positive on the active interval. The paper fixes $\max\gamma=1$; this condition allows any smaller nonzero seed. The vector transport equation and nonvanishing are recorded explicitly, although they follow for a transported nonzero carrier. Frequency normalization is separate.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent:
The domain is represented by periodic fields on $\mathbb R^3$. Require $T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, smooth odd divergence-free $U$ with flow $X$, and Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\mathsf D$. Operator norms of $
abla U$, $D_aX$ and its inverse are at most $\mathsf D$. The pressure $p$ is smooth and periodic; $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$ is odd, supported in $|\xi|\le4\mathsf D$, and has supremum norm at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Finally $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. The time derivative is within $[0,T]$. Unlike §5.1, this condition imposes neither $\int p=0$ nor $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((
abla U)^2)$, and it does not assume $\operatorname{div}R_U=0$. The numbered results separately add $T>0$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution: Given the parent flow, its gradient $M$, transported covector $\kappa$ and forcing profile $f$, a transverse solution on $[0,T]$ satisfies $V_t+MV+\kappa\partial_s\pi=f$, $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=0$ and $V(0,a,s)=0$. The phase pressure is also normalized by $\langle\pi\rangle_s=0$. These are smooth profiles with phase period one and the simultaneous label-phase translation law giving a periodic physical field. Time derivatives hold the label fixed. This is the problem used for (1.12) after its specified forcing is inserted. The definition describes a solution; it does not assert existence, uniqueness or a bound.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: The paper’s $C_p$ is stored at index $p-1$; the physical expansion sets $C_1=0$. The field $Y_p=V_p+C_p$ groups the new transverse velocity with the divergence correction produced by $V_{p-1}$. This is the convention at the start of §5.5, reflecting the extra frequency gain of the correction. The sum itself imposes no equation; its size and constraints follow from the expansion equations and Theorem 5.6.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd: For an indexed family of profiles, the formal definition gives $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ in the paper's notation. Here $C_p$ is generated by the preceding oscillation $V_{p-1}$: the stored correction index is one smaller than the paper index. The formula defines the level field used in the quadratic interactions of §1.3 and §5.5. It does not impose that $B_p$ is phase independent or that $V_p$ is transverse; these belong to the expansion equations. At index zero, subtraction is truncated to zero, so the intended mathematical use is at levels $p\ge1$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection: Profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$, with phase period one and $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$. Nonvanishing of the transported covector is supplied by the parent geometry. The correction is $C[V]=\mathbf d\times Q[V]$, with $Q[V]=-\partial_s^{-1}((\kappa\times V)/|\kappa|^2)$. For zero-mean transverse profiles it gives $V+C[V]=\widetilde{\mathbf d}\times Q[V]$, as used in §5.5. The formal operation acts on the oscillatory part of a general profile; the divergence identity requires the zero-mean and transversality assumptions.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion: For depth $P\ge0$, the formal definition is $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$, using the paper's indices. Thus the correction of $V_P$ remains even though the next oscillation is absent. When $C_1=0$ and $P\ge1$, regrouping gives $W=\sum_{p=1}^PZ_p+C_{P+1}$; when $P=0$, the sum is empty and equals zero. The definition accepts arbitrary additive families. To obtain the approximate velocity, one evaluates the profiles at $s=k_*\cdot a$, passes to physical coordinates and adds the parent. Differential equations, divergence cancellation and size estimates are additional facts.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure: The depth $P$ is a nonnegative integer; an empty sum is zero, while Proposition 5.4 uses $P\ge2$. The profile pressure is $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^{P}(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, as in Proposition 5.4. In an admissible expansion the oscillatory pressures have zero phase mean, the mean pressures are phase independent, and $\bar q_1=0$. Those equations and normalizations belong to the construction; this expression simply adds the selected pressure components.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm: For a field $f(t,a,s)$ and time set $I$, this expression sums the suprema of $\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^j(\tau(t)f)$ over $t\in I$, $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, for $|\alpha|+j\le n$. Each multi-index occurs once. Only label and phase are differentiated, so the time multiplier is applied after differentiation. For $\tau=\gamma^{-1}$ this is the weighted norm of Appendix D. The definition itself supplies neither boundedness nor positivity of $\gamma$; the analytic statements supply these conditions before using it as a norm.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leading: For a seed field $\mathbf a(t,a)$, define $A_1(t,a,s)=g(a)\mathbf a(t,a)F_h(s)$ with $g(a)=\chi(|a|/\ell_*)$. The formalization selects a particular smooth radial cutoff $\chi$ and the periodic phase profile $F_h$ constructed earlier. This is the unswitched leading wave in §5.1; the time cutoff is introduced later as $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$. The formula itself assumes no differential equation for the seed and no positive radius or width. Its intended smooth localized interpretation uses $\ell_*>0$, $0<h\le1$, and the seed regularity on $[t_0,T]$ supplied in the application.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource: This defines the source for $p\ge2$ using $Y_i=V_i+C_i$ and $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$; subtraction of natural-number indices is truncated at zero outside that range. The source $H_p$ contains $(\partial_t+M)C_p+\mathbf d\mathsf p_{p-1}$ and the two interaction sums of (5.26). At level two it subtracts the activation contribution of the curl correction, recovering (5.25). The correction $C_p$ is already known from $V_{p-1}$, so the source does not depend on the new transverse velocity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource: At level $p$, the formal definition is $\overline f_p=-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R$, where $H_p$ is the source assembled before solving for the new mean and $R$ is the supplied parent residual. In the geometric application $R=R_U\circ X$ is independent of phase. The negative sign makes the mean correction cancel the averaged error, and level two is the only place where the previous parent's residual is inserted. This is the right side of the equation described in §1.3. The definition does not solve that equation or impose the endpoint conditions selecting its initial velocity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource: For an arbitrary preliminary source $H_p$, phase averaging is the integral over one period; centering is an algebraic operation, not an existence statement. The forcing $f_p=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s)$ is the centered term in (5.27). Its sign cancels the oscillatory part of $H_p$ in the momentum equation. The additional forcing $f_p^S$ is formed only after the mean solve, and the transverse equation uses their sum; centering the preliminary source alone does not include that transport.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.radius: The formal radius is $\ell_*=(\mathsf D^a)^{-1}$, where $a$ is a nonnegative integer. In the parent regime $\mathsf D\ge2$, this is positive; choosing $a\ge3$ gives the paper’s $\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-3}$. The later estimates first fix a sufficiently large threshold for $a$, then quantify over all larger integer exponents. The radius does not change with derivative order or expansion depth. The definition also accepts $\mathsf D=0$: since the reciprocal of zero is zero, it then gives zero for $a>0$ and one for $a=0$. Those values are excluded by the parent assumptions.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder: The stored correction is indexed by its generating velocity, so the paper’s $C_{P+1}$ is the stored correction with index $P$. The expression is (5.30): the two final linear terms, label interactions with $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions with $i+j\ge P+2$. Both indices run through $P+1$, where only the final correction remains. The activation error is separate. The expansion equations are needed to identify this expression with the uncanceled momentum residual.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource: The formal definition gives $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^{p}(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$, with $Y_j=V_j+C_j$ in paper notation. In particular, at $p=2$ it is $-(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$ when $C_1=0$, the extra term in (1.12). The sum is empty below level two. At every included index $p+1-i\ge1$, so nonnegative-integer subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction. For phase-independent $B_i,\kappa$ and differentiable periodic $Y_j$, its phase average vanishes. These properties are not imposed by the formula alone; they come from the geometric profiles and expansion equations.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm: For a smooth profile on $[0,T]$, this is the sum of suprema of $\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^j f/\gamma(t)$ on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, with $|\alpha|+j\le n$ and each multi-index once. No time derivative of $\gamma$ is taken. The profile is one-periodic in phase and satisfies the coupled label-translation law. The definition permits arbitrary $\gamma$ and interprets division by zero as zero; applications require continuous strictly positive $\gamma$, making it the ordinary weighted norm. Values outside $[0,T]$ are fixed to zero without asserting smoothness across the endpoints.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.waveVector: The formal vector is $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$, with reference time zero. When $X$ is the smooth parent flow, the inverse derivative identity makes this $(D_aX(t,a))^{-T}k_*$, exactly the transported field in §5.1. The argument $a$ is a parent label, not the physical point. The formula alone does not require $k_*\ne0$ or guarantee invertibility: these enter through the parent and activation hypotheses. Likewise, nonvanishing and the frequency comparisons (5.3) are proved separately. Outside differentiability, the formal derivative expression is assigned its default value zero.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.weight: Given a frequency $\lambda$ and central seed $\mathbf a(t,0)$, define $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. This is the weight used in the active-interval profile norms: $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$ measures spatial and phase derivatives of $f/\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$. Because $\gamma$ depends only on time, those derivatives do not act on it. The definition itself proves neither positivity nor an upper bound. The parent frequency $\lambda\ge1$, nonzero central seed, and normalization imposed elsewhere give $0<\gamma\le1$. It does not impose the paper’s stronger equality $\max_{[t_0,T]}\gamma=1$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.width: The formal width is the real power $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. Under the parent condition $\lambda\ge1$, this gives $0<h\le1$, as required for the chosen periodic profile $F_h$. In the finite profile norms, every phase derivative carries a factor $h$; converting to a physical derivative introduces $|k_*|h^{-1}$. With $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$ this is at most $\mathsf D\lambda^{3/2}$. The width definition does not assert these inequalities without their frequency assumptions. Combined with central amplitude scale $\lambda^{-3/4}$ and $\|F_h\|_\infty=O(h)$, it yields the leading velocity scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_divergence: Let $U$ be the smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$ and its coefficient data. Suppose a smooth profile $W(t,a,s)$ has zero total profile divergence, $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$, where $\widetilde{\mathbf d}=(D_aX)^{-T}(\nabla_a+k_*\partial_s)$. Then $V(t,x)=U(t,x)+W(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}V=0$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. The formal statement receives the full parent hypotheses of §5.1, including its quantitative bounds, although this implication uses the smooth flow and incompressibility. It is the divergence step in Lemma 5.8; zero label divergence alone would not remove the phase contribution.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual:
For the smooth periodic parent $U,p$ and its flow $X$, let smooth profiles $W,\mathsf P,R,F$ satisfy $(\partial_t+M)W+(W\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf d})W+\widetilde{\mathbf d}\mathsf P+R=F$. Require $R(t,a,s)=R_U(t,X_{0,t}(a))$, where $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$. Then the momentum residual of $V=U+W^
atural$, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ is exactly $F^
atural$ on $[0,T]$, with evaluation through the inverse label and phase $k_*\cdot a$. This is the coordinate implication applied in Lemma 5.8 with $F=R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. The formal statement assumes the profile momentum identity and the complete parent data; it does not derive the finite hierarchy equations.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_smooth:
Let $U,p$ be the smooth periodic parent fields on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, with flow $X$. For smooth velocity and pressure profiles satisfying phase periodicity and $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$, the fields $U+W^
atural$ and $p+\mathsf P^
atural$ are smooth and periodic, where $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$. The formal statement assumes the full quantitative parent conditions, but no hierarchy equation for the chosen profiles. It proves the regularity part of Lemma 5.8. It does not assert oddness, incompressibility or a particular momentum residual; those require symmetry and equations in addition to smoothness.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_norm_le_wNorm: Let a smooth profile $g(t,a,s)$ vanish for $t<t_0$ within $[0,T]$, and let $\gamma$ be positive continuous with $\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. For any map $Y(t,x)$, $|g(t,Y(t,x),k_*\cdot Y(t,x))|\le\|g\|_{[0],\gamma}$ for all $t\in[0,T]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. The order-zero weighted norm is the supremum of $|g|/\gamma$ over active times, labels and phases. No smoothness or invertibility of $Y$ is needed for this pointwise comparison. Lemma 5.8 uses $Y=X_{t,0}$ and $g=W_{\rm osc}$; the additional scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$ comes from the separate hierarchy estimate.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd:
Assume the localized seed, finite expansion, transverse inverse, hierarchy and physical evaluation results, together with oddness of all admissible expansions. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over the smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent of §5.1, with stable positive central coupling, $0<\gamma\le1$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the formal statement derives the full assertions of Lemma 5.8. These are smooth periodic $V=U+W^
atural$ and $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$, odd divergence-free $V$, the exact residual $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$, and the velocity and residual estimates (5.47)–(5.48). The residual bound retains $\sup_{[t_0,T]}|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}|\gamma$ alongside $\lambda^{-2P/3}$. This is a conditional assembly theorem; the separate symmetry result supplies the assumed oddness from uniqueness of the expansion.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelConstant_indep: Fix $P'\le P$ and the same numerical recurrence coefficient $K$ in both depths. The equality holds for every $q\le P'$. The numerical constant for a level is unchanged when the surrounding expansion is extended to a larger depth. The interaction pairs at the earlier levels are identical, so induction gives equality of their constants. This justifies the dependence $C_{n,p}$ in Theorem 5.6; it does not assert a bound uniform in $p$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence: Assume a depth-$P$ expansion with smooth profiles, the parent band and deformation bounds, the residual and coercivity bounds, and a stable central seed with positive coupling and $0<\gamma\le1$. The parent, mean, transverse, and correction estimates give a recurrence for the actual profile norms and a direct estimate for the remainder. Phase integration replaces the fast derivative in the mean source by a label divergence. One parent exponent suffices independently of derivative order and depth, while the order and finite-depth constants retain their allowed dependence.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oddExpansions_of: Assume Proposition 5.4, including uniqueness of the retained profiles. Over the smooth odd periodic parent of §5.1, take a seed with even dependence on the label and an admissible depth-$P\ge2$ expansion. Reflect $(a,s)$ to $(-a,-s)$, reverse the sign of velocity profiles and preserve the sign of pressure profiles. The reflected family satisfies the same defining equations and prescribed data. Uniqueness therefore makes the retained velocity expansion odd under this reflection. After composition with the odd inverse parent flow, its Eulerian perturbation is odd. This statement proves symmetry of the expansion; it does not derive its quantitative estimates or bound its residual.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm: The profile is smooth and phase periodic, with the coupled label-translation law; the weight is continuous on the compact active interval. For a profile vanishing before $t_0$, its unweighted norm on $[0,T]$ is at most its weighted norm on $[t_0,T]$ when $0<\gamma\le1$. The vanishing assumption matters because the time intervals differ. The remainder proof applies this to terms containing oscillations; products of two means are estimated directly in the unweighted norm.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general: Let $\ell_*,h>0$ and let the time weight $\gamma$ be positive. Suppose all finite norms of $f/\gamma$ exist, and the coefficients of label and phase differentiation have finite order-$j$ bounds $N_c(j)$ and $N_k(j)$. Assuming the finite-norm product estimate, the sum over all ordered sequences of $m$ physical coordinate derivatives is bounded by $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}[C_j(9N_c(j)\ell_*^{-1}+3N_k(j)h^{-1})]\,\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The formal conclusion also includes finiteness of these differentiated norms. With inverse-flow coefficients and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, this gives the derivative cost in Lemma 5.7. The product for $m=0$ is one; its order constants are those of the product estimate, not new assumptions on the parent.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep: Let $f$ be independent of phase, $\ell_*,h>0$, and $\gamma>0$. Assume finite weighted profile norms at every order and finite order-$j$ coefficient bounds $N_c(j),N_k(j)$ for the label and phase parts of the derivative operator. Given the finite-norm product estimate, the sum of the weighted norms after all ordered sequences of $m$ physical coordinate derivatives is at most $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}[C_j9N_c(j)\ell_*^{-1}]\,\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The phase-coefficient bounds remain formal premises, but no $N_k(j)h^{-1}$ factor appears in the conclusion because phase derivatives vanish. This is the improved mean estimate used in Lemma 5.7. The conclusion includes finiteness of all differentiated order-zero norms.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.L: For a real-valued frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, the formal definition is $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. This is the gain parameter in (1.14); in particular $L_{j+1}$ uses $\lambda_{j+2}$, which matters in Lemma 1.3. The formula is defined even without a positive-frequency hypothesis. The logarithm is assigned the value zero at zero and is extended to negative arguments using their absolute value. In the paper’s schedule all frequencies exceed one, so this convention is inactive and $L_j>0$. The formula alone provides neither that positivity nor any bound on the gain.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.ε: For the frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, put $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. The formal definition assigns $\varepsilon_j=1/L_{j+1}^2$, agreeing with $\varepsilon_{j-1}=L_j^{-2}$ for $j\ge2$ in (1.14). Consequently $\varepsilon_j$ depends on $\lambda_{j+2}$, not $\lambda_{j+1}$. The formal formula also assigns a value at index zero, which this part of the paper does not use. Division by zero is assigned the value zero, so a zero gain would give a zero ratio, not an infinite one. The positive-frequency schedule supplies positive gains; separate estimates make these positive ratios small enough for amplification.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ: For a positive frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, put $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. At each wave index $j\ge1$, the formal definition is $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^3$, the half-length used in $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$. The formula uses a real exponent $-1/8$ and an integer cube. It is also assigned a value at index zero: subtraction of one from a nonnegative integer gives zero there, so it uses $\lambda_0$. The paper does not use that extra value. Positivity, decay of $\tau_j$, and the endpoint relation require separate assertions; this formula alone supplies none of them.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.SmoothTerminalExtension: The formal condition asks for an open set containing $\{T\}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ and a field $g$ smooth jointly on its union with $[0,T)\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$. The field is periodic under every integer spatial translation and equals $u$ on that entire preterminal punctured slab. Thus it descends to a smooth extension through the terminal slice of the punctured torus. The field is defined everywhere, but smoothness is required only on the stated union; its other values are unconstrained. This condition neither asserts an Euler equation after $T$ nor extends a pressure. It specifies what an extension means and does not prove one exists.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Write $M=DU\circ X$, $K=DX^TDX$ and $\Omega=DX^T(M^T-M)DX$. For every prescribed exponent $C_A$ and $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$, a sufficiently large radius exponent gives $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$ for $m\ge1$, with finite coefficient norms. The radius threshold may depend on $C_A$ but not the parent or derivative order. The displayed polynomial bound on $A$ is assumed.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Let $B=DXv$, $v=z_t$, solve the mean equation with $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$; set $g=DX^T\bar f$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, finite scaled half-Hölder norm of $g$ at order $n$ implies finiteness for $v$ and $\|v\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|g\|_{[n],1/2}$. Time runs over $[0,T]$. No derivative is lost here; the later supremum-norm estimate uses one more source derivative.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59: For each integer $m\ge0$, the assertion asks for a nonnegative constant $C_m$ such that every continuous bilinear map $B:E\times F\to G$ between real normed spaces satisfies $\|B(f,g)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_m\|B\|\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$ whenever $f:\mathbb R^3\to E$ and $g:\mathbb R^3\to F$ belong to $C^{m,1/2}$. The output’s Hölder regularity is also asserted. The constant is chosen before the spaces, fields and bilinear map. This states a generalization of (5.59); scalar multiplication and the tensor products used in §5.7 are particular cases. It does not require periodicity.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_D_2: Let $0<\ell_*\le1$ and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, where $X$ is any real normed space. Assume all derivatives through order $n+1$ are uniformly bounded in time and label. The formal statement proves $\|c\|_{[n]}\le\|c\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|c\|_{[n+1]}$ and establishes finiteness of the Hölder quantities. At each order $m$ it also proves $\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}(\ell_*^m|c|_m+\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1})$. Each multi-index is counted once. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; their sum is equivalent within a factor two. Thus the explicit constant four yields the paper's unspecified constant after the chosen norm convention is accounted for.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8: The formal statement asks for parameters, an inductive construction, a constant and a real time $T$ satisfying the conclusions of Theorem 7.1. These include smooth odd divergence-free periodic stage velocities, the residual and central-wave bounds, summable corrections, shrinking oscillation supports, and $0<T<S_j$ for every stage, with $t_j\to T$. Thus $T$ is the paper’s common accumulation time. This declaration specifies an existence assertion; the adjoining proof establishes it from Theorem 7.1. Its conclusion contains no limiting field and no uniform convergence on $[0,T]$. It represents only the initial choice in Section 8, not the whole opening paragraph.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.corollary_8_3: Given a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit $u,p$ from Proposition 8.1, assume bounded velocity, central vorticity blow-up, and fixed $c>0,C$ with $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ throughout every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. The formal statement concludes maximality at $T_\infty>0$, equality with the lifespan of every other maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$, and divergence of both integrals in (1.2). The quantitative bound is included in the formal Proposition 8.2, although not in its printed statement. This declaration specifies the implication; its proof uses crossing durations instead of a general continuation criterion. The integrals are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals over the half-open lifespan.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_1_3: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, and $\mathcal B(s)>0$ satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$. Suppose $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. Then $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for $j\ge1$. Thus the last expression is exactly (1.15), since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$. The formal statement omits threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination from §1.5; the arithmetic result therefore applies under fewer assumptions.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_1: Let $J$ be a time interval on which relative derivatives are uniquely determined. Suppose $D$ is differentiable, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$, $D'+D^2$ is symmetric, and $k'=-D^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+p_{\rm w}k$, where $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$. Unlike the paper, the formal statement requires neither a smooth odd periodic profile nor its normalization; the Euler identity also allows $k=0$, using zero for division by zero. The interval derivative includes one-sided endpoint derivatives.

notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_3_1: The formal statement asks whether the constructed bump-based families $F_h,P_h$ have all properties of Lemma 3.1. For $0<h\le1$, these are smoothness and period one, oddness of $F_h$, $P_h'=F_h$, zero phase mean of $P_h$, $F_h'(0)=1$, $-Ch\le F_h'\le1$ and $|F_h|\le Ch$. The exponent is integral and can be negative. This assertion fixes particular families, making it more specific than the paper's existence statement; its definition is distinct from the proof that follows.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_4_1: Let $u$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$ on $[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$. Set $F=D_aX$, $M=(\nabla u)\circ X$, $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)$, $K=F^TF$, and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. If $H^\#\le I$ as quadratic forms, then for each label and every $z\in H^1_0$, with $\xi=Fz$, $\int H^\#\xi\cdot\xi\le\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$ and $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\ge\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$. The formal statement represents $z$ by $Jv$ with $v\in L^2$ and $\int v=0$, so no test paths are lost. Symmetry of $H^\#$ is unnecessary. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_10: Let $V=U+W^\natural$ arise from a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Require $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, a nonzero transverse seed satisfying (5.5), $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. For every smooth periodic divergence-free $v$ with each spatial derivative through order two at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$, a flow of $V+v$ exists and every flow has forward and inverse derivative norms at most $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{1/4}$. The derivative bounds are separate, weaker premises than the paper’s summed $C^2$ bound. Constants precede the parent. The parent pressure need not be the normalized Poisson pressure.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: Assume a smooth odd solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual $R_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Let $0\le t_0<T$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, and a nonzero transverse central seed have relative growth at most $\mathsf D$, normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$ and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, nearby seeds obey $|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ and positive coupling. Supported transverse solutions obey $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. Zero-initial centered forcing gives $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$; the leading wave has bound $C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4}$. The first estimate requires full-interval profiles; the paper permits active-interval data. Pressure and amplitude assumptions are broader; the envelope is fixed.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, transverse $V$ satisfies $\|C[V]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1}\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. If $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, the same factor bounds $(\partial_t+M)C[V]+\mathbf d\mathsf p$ by the sum of the next-order norms of $V,f$. The profiles are smooth and $V,f$ have zero phase mean on all $[0,T]$; transversality, the equation and pressure normalization concern $[t_0,T]$. Smooth representatives of the homogeneous leading wave are also proved to exist. Thus full-interval assumptions accompany broader pressure and amplitude hypotheses.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_7: For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$ with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, residual size $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and coercivity $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$, impose the central seed conditions (5.5), $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$ and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Take $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ sufficiently small and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. A smooth profile with the combined lattice translation law, independent of phase outside the envelope, satisfies $\|D^mf^\natural\|\le C_m(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})^m\gamma(t)\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$ and the $C^{m,1/2}$ bound using $m+1$. Here the derivative norm sums ordered coordinate sequences. The weighted estimates hold on $[t_0,T]$. Both estimates hold unweighted on $[0,T]$, and phase-independent fields omit $\lambda^{3/2}$. The target is any real normed space; constants precede the parent. The formal profile already incorporates continuation across cells.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8:
For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, require deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$. Take $\lambda\ge1$, a nonzero transverse seed satisfying (5.5), $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, and a depth-$P\ge2$ finite expansion with sufficiently small envelope. If $C_{m step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, then $V=U+W^
atural$ is smooth, odd and divergence free, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ is smooth, and their residual is $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$. The bounds are $C_{0,P}\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-5/4}$ for the oscillatory supremum, $C_{m,P}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{3(m+1)/2-5/4}$ and $C_{m,P}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{-5/2}$ for oscillatory and mean Hölder norms, and $C_{m step}\lambda^2(\lambda^{-2P/3}+\|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}\gamma\|_\infty)$ for the residual. All hold on $[0,T]$. Constants precede the parent; the pressure class and peak normalization are broader than the paper’s.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_9: For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, require deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Take a nonzero transverse seed satisfying (5.5), $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, and a depth-$P\ge2$ finite expansion with sufficiently small envelope. Under $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the assertion gives $D_x^2\mathsf P^\natural\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$ and $\|D V(t,0)-D U(t,0)-\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ on $[t_0,T]$. The first is a quadratic-form upper bound, the second an operator-norm bound. Constants precede the parent and expansion. Neither zero-mean Poisson normalization of $p$ nor attainment of $\max\gamma=1$ is required.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1: For $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$ and $T>0$, assume $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, where $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$. The formal statement asserts existence of the first central wave: initial covector $\lambda e_1$, positive initial amplitude along $e_2$, nonzero transversality, the wave equations and attained peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$ on $[0,T]$. It also asserts that every such wave has initial strength in $[\lambda^{1/4}/2,\lambda^{1/4}]$, and, for every $\mathsf D\ge2$, obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for transverse solutions and ordered times, with $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$. Here $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. The matrix norm is the operator norm. This declaration states the proposition; its proof is linked separately.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2: For $H=\mathbb R^3$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P$; for $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal Q$ removes the time average. Suppose $B:\mathbb T^3\to\mathcal L(H)$ is Lipschitz with constant $L\ge0$ and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$, $\mu>0$, for all vectors in the first case and zero-time-mean paths in the second. Then $\mathcal RB$ is invertible on its projected half-Hölder space with bound $C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p$. The constants are chosen before $B$, with integer $p\ge0$. If $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, $k\ge1$, the same inverse preserves that class. The paper requires the stronger base hypothesis $B\in C^{1,1/2}$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: On $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, let $S_\Lambda$ have symbol $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$, where $\psi$ is smooth, even, between zero and one, equal to one on the unit ball and zero outside the radius-two ball. For every $\Lambda>0$, the formal statement gives parity, frequency support, derivative commutation, the operator bounds, and (B.1)–(B.2), with constants chosen before the frequency, fields and target spaces. Spatial derivatives and norms are measured on periodic lifts. Bernstein's sum counts each multi-index once and permits any real normed target. The measurable-input $L^\infty$ clause is complex Banach-valued; the real-velocity branch assumes continuity. Spatial commutation covers all complex orders and one real coordinate derivative, with a separate first-time-derivative clause on smooth closed slabs. Higher real orders require iteration. The supplied description uses derivative-tensor Hölder sums; the underlying higher-order norm definition is absent and its normalization is not independently checked here. The paper assumes radiality and $\Lambda\ge1$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: Let $\ell_*,h>0$, let $\gamma(t)>0$ on a chosen time set, and let the fields be smooth in $(a,s)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with the required derivatives uniformly bounded. The formal statement proves (D.3) with label constant three, the weighted bilinear product estimate (D.4), and (D.5) with primitive constant two; it also proves that the output norms are finite. The norm sums one term per mixed multi-index, after division by $\gamma$. Products may be any continuous bilinear map, with its operator norm included in the constant. Phase averaging and inversion require period one and a real Banach target; inversion also requires zero phase average. Neither periodicity nor zero average is needed for differentiation or products. The phase-independent Hölder product estimate uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; changing to their sum only alters the constant.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: Assume $\mathsf D\ge1$ and smooth phase-independent coefficients with $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$. The formal statement uses nonnegative integer exponents. For inputs with exponents $q,r$, a bilinear product of norm at most one has exponent $2\max(q,r)$. In a complete real normed algebra, pointwise invertibility and $\|c^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D^e$ give exponent $3\max(q,e)$. Output constants are selected after the input constants and value spaces, but before $\mathsf D$, the time set and fields. Finally, $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-q}$ gives $\|c\|_{[n]}\le C'_n\mathsf D^q$ and $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C'_m\mathsf D^{2q}\ell_*$ for $m\ge1$. Rounding the paper's fixed real exponent upward changes both this radius condition and its concluding powers; it does not reproduce that clause literally.

notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$.
