A field with $\|D^mf\|\le C_m^{\prime}A_f\mathsf D^m$ satisfies $\|D_a^m(f\circ X)\|\le C_mA_f\mathsf D^{Cm}$. If $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-C}$, the scaled sums satisfy (5.8). One exponent works at every order; operator norms replace coordinate sums.

Take a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-\nabla R_U\le I$. Require (5.5), $\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, small envelope and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, where $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$. For smooth radial $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $|\xi|\le1$ and zero on $|\xi|>2$, and every $\Lambda\ge1$, $u=S_\Lambda V$ and its zero-mean Poisson pressure exist. Both $u,R_u$ are odd and divergence free, with Fourier radii $2\Lambda,4\Lambda$. Put $\varepsilon=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$ and $e=C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon$. Then $\|u-V\|_{C_tC^{2,1/2}}\le K_P\varepsilon$, the summed residual and pressure-Hessian errors are at most $e$, and $D^2(p-p_U)\le(C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}+e)I$. Constants precede the parent; $2-P$ is an integer exponent.

Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. For a smooth periodic phase-independent solution $B_t+MB+\mathbf d\bar q=\bar f$, require $B=DXz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. At sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|\bar f\|_{[n+1]}$ for every $n$. These are scaled label-derivative suprema on all of $[0,T]$. The exponent is chosen before the parent and order. This estimates existing solutions; it does not set $B(0)=0$.

Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, the projected seed exists, and every depth $P\ge2$ admits a unique family of retained velocities and normalized pressures satisfying the mean and transverse recursions. For $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$ and $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^P(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$ and the momentum residual is $R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. The oscillations and their sources vanish before activation and outside the envelope; there the remainder is phase independent. Means need not vanish before activation. Smoothness is on the closed slab; no continuation across its endpoints is asserted.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: For every common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, the formal statement asserts existence of smooth periodic velocity and mean-zero pressure solving Euler on $[0,T_\infty)$. The limiting datum $u(0)$ is smooth, odd and divergence free; $U_j(0)\to u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$. For each $S<T_\infty$, convergence to $u$ is uniform on $[0,S]$ in every such spatial norm, and $u$ remains odd. Any maximal solution with the same data and a finite lifespan must last at least to $T_\infty$ and agree there. Unlike the paper’s formulation, existence of a general maximal solution is not assumed or concluded. This declaration states the assertion; a separate theorem proves it. The precise numerical Hölder norm is defined in an omitted file.

For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the formal statement asserts bounded velocity on $[0,T_\infty)$ and the full limit $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. It also asserts fixed real $c>0,C$ such that $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. Here the spatial domain is represented by period-one fields on $\mathbb R^3$, and the velocity norm is the essential supremum on one unit cell. The interval estimate is extra information beyond the printed Proposition 8.2. This declaration specifies the assertion; its proof and its application to integral divergence are separate.

For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth periodic Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the formal statement asserts both limits in Proposition 8.4. For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and integer $m\ge0$, $u(t)$ and its time derivative converge uniformly on $K$ with all spatial derivatives through order $m$, as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. Each limiting field is $C^m$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. The removed lattice is precisely the set of representatives of the torus origin. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T_\infty)$. This declaration states the implication; it does not itself prove it. No single jointly smooth extension through the terminal time is required by this conclusion.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.remark_1_2: There exist smooth odd divergence-free data $u_0$ on $\mathbb T^3$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, with $0<T_*<\infty$, bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and divergent time integrals of both gradient and vorticity norms. Velocity and its time derivative converge in every spatial $C^m$ norm on compact sets away from the origin. The velocity also extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from that point. Any maximal solution from $u_0$ has the same lifespan and velocity. The extension is periodic and need not solve Euler after $T_*$. This is the existential assertion of Remark 1.2, not an extension theorem for every singular solution.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_1_1: There exist smooth odd divergence-free periodic data $u_0$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$, with finite $T_*>0$. Velocity remains uniformly bounded, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and the time integrals of $\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty$ and $\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty$ both diverge. For every compact set away from the torus origin and every $m\ge0$, velocity and its time derivative converge in $C^m$. The formal statement further spells out the classical uniqueness implicit in the paper: every maximal solution from $u_0$ has endpoint $T_*$ and agrees with $u$ before it. Fields are periodic functions on $\mathbb R^3$; pressure has zero spatial mean.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_4_2: Let $0<T\le1$ and let $U$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$. Put $F=D_aX$, $M=(D_xU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$ and assume $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. For every $L\in C([0,T];C^{0,1/2})$, the formal statement gives unique $z,v=z_t,c,\nabla\phi$ satisfying $Kv-\int_0^t\Omega v+L=c+\nabla\phi$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, with $z,v,c$ divergence free. Only the gradient of $\phi$ is unique. A polynomial in uniform bounds for $F^{-1},M,K,\Omega$ and the first label derivatives of $K,\Omega$ bounds $v$ and $(\mathbb PK(t))^{-1}\mathbb P$. Smooth force sources yield smooth $b=(Fv)\circ X^{-1}$ solving the linearized Euler equation and $b(0)=c$. The paper uses larger $C^{1,1/2}$ coefficient norms. The $C^{0,1/2}$ norm is the maximum of the supremum norm and Hölder seminorm.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Fix a sufficiently small radius $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and a depth-$P$ expansion, $P\ge2$. If $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, then at every order the transverse velocity, forcing and $\lambda$ times pressure have size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$; means and mean sources have size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2-2(p-2)/3}$; $C_{p+1}$ has size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-9/4-2(p-1)/3}$. The finite sums satisfy (5.37), and $\|R_P\|_{[m]}\le C_{m,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$. Means use the whole interval, oscillations the active weighted norm. The same exponent works for all orders, levels and depths.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: For every smooth radial Fourier cutoff and integer $a_0$, the formal statement chooses $b\ge1$, $a\ge a_0$ and fixed-order majorants before an admissible threshold $\mathcal B$. Every such threshold permits the construction for all sufficiently large $N$. It asserts smooth odd divergence-free periodic velocities on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$, with $\|U_j\|_\infty,\|(D_aX_j)^{\pm1}\|_\infty\le\lambda_j$, $\|R_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ and $D^2\pi_j\le(\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1})I$. The central splitting has error $\le\lambda_j^{-1/4}$; at $t_{j+1}$, $\eta_j/\nu_j=\varepsilon_j$, $\pi\le\nu_j\le4\pi$ and $C^{-1}\lambda_j^{1/4}\le\sigma_j\le C\lambda_j^{1/4}L_{j+1}^2$, with $C=18e^3$. Localized increments satisfy $\|O_j\|_\infty,\|U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for $m\le q_j$, and $t_j\to T_\infty\in(0,S_j)$. Each increment is identified with its finite expansion and Fourier truncation. The central amplitude is identified with the seed; the central covector is not identified with its transported counterpart, and first-wave directions and attained normalization are absent. The exponent quantifier is $\forall a_0\,\exists a\ge a_0$. Hölder estimates are stated at each time; their exact spatial norm definition is absent. This declaration states the assertion, not its proof.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1:
On $[0,1]	imes\mathbb T^3$, let $K$ be symmetric and $\Omega$ skew-symmetric, continuous in time in $C^{0,1/2}$, spatially differentiable, with uniform value and first derivative bounds. Assume $K\ge\kappa I$, $\kappa>0$, and $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\ge\mu\int|z_t|^2$, $\mu>0$, for every $H^1_0$ path at each label. Every $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$ gives unique $z,v=z_t,c,
abla\phi$ solving $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+
abla\phi$, with divergence-free $z,c$ and zero endpoints. Moreover $\|v\|_0\le CQ^p\|L\|_0$, where $Jv(t)=\int_0^tv$ and $Q=2+\kappa^{-1}+\mu^{-1}+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1$; the subscripts give the uniform value and first derivative bounds. Smooth data give smooth $z,c,

notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_13: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Write $M=DU\circ X$, $K=DX^TDX$ and $\Omega=DX^T(M^T-M)DX$. For every prescribed exponent $C_A$ and $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$, a sufficiently large radius exponent gives $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$ for $m\ge1$, with finite coefficient norms. The radius threshold may depend on $C_A$ but not the parent or derivative order. The displayed polynomial bound on $A$ is assumed.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_14: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Let $B=DXv$, $v=z_t$, solve the mean equation with $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$; set $g=DX^T\bar f$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, finite scaled half-Hölder norm of $g$ at order $n$ implies finiteness for $v$ and $\|v\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|g\|_{[n],1/2}$. Time runs over $[0,T]$. No derivative is lost here; the later supremum-norm estimate uses one more source derivative.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_59: For every integer $m\ge0$, there is a constant $C_m$ independent of the real normed spaces $E,F,G$ and the continuous bilinear map $B:E\times F\to G$, such that $f,g\in C^{m,1/2}(\mathbb R^3)$ imply $B(f,g)\in C^{m,1/2}$ and $\|B(f,g)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_m\|B\|\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$. This theorem proves the formal assertion corresponding to (5.59), with all target-space and product choices included. The proof permits $C_m=3(m+1)2^m$. Scalar multiplication and the tensor products used in the cutoff residual are special cases; no periodicity assumption is needed.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_D_2: Let $0<\ell_*\le1$ and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, where $X$ is any real normed space. Assume all derivatives through order $n+1$ are uniformly bounded in time and label. The formal statement proves $\|c\|_{[n]}\le\|c\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|c\|_{[n+1]}$ and establishes finiteness of the Hölder quantities. At each order $m$ it also proves $\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}(\ell_*^m|c|_m+\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1})$. Each multi-index is counted once. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; their sum is equivalent within a factor two. Thus the explicit constant four yields the paper's unspecified constant after the chosen norm convention is accounted for.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.section8_setting: This theorem proves that there are admissible parameters, an inductive construction, a constant and a finite positive time $T_\infty$ satisfying Theorem 7.1. The same smooth periodic stage velocities have the stated residual, support, increment and central-wave bounds, and their activation times converge to $T_\infty$ while each stage lasts beyond it. This supplies the setting selected at the start of Section 8. The formal conclusion stops at that existence assertion: it does not introduce $w$ or assert uniform convergence on the closed interval. The continuous terminal velocity is established by a separate result using summability of the increments.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: For smooth odd periodic velocities $U_j$ on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$, their flows $X_j$, zero-mean pressures $\pi_j$ and residuals $R_j$, this condition requires frequency support $\le2\lambda_j^5$, $\|U_j\|_\infty,\|(D_aX_j)^{\pm1}\|_\infty\le\lambda_j$, $\|R_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ and $D^2\pi_j\le(\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1})I$. At the origin, the central splitting has error $\le\lambda_j^{-1/4}$; at $t_{j+1}$, $\eta_j/\nu_j=\varepsilon_j$, $\pi\le\nu_j\le4\pi$ and $C^{-1}\lambda_j^{1/4}\le\sigma_j\le C\lambda_j^{1/4}L_{j+1}^2$, with $C\ge2$. Times satisfy $0=t_1=t_2<t_3<\cdots\to T_\infty\in(0,S_j)$. At each time, oscillations are supported within distance $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ of the integer lattice, with $\|O_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ and $\|U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for $m\le q_j$; $O_j=0$ before activation for $j\ge2$. These requirements neither construct the fields nor identify the oscillation with the finite expansion. Continuity in the time-dependent Hölder norm is not separately asserted; its exact spatial norm definition is absent.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: For wave $j\ge1$, take parent $U_{j-1}$ on $[0,S_j]$, frequency $\lambda_j$, parent bound $\mathsf D=\lambda_{j-1}^9$, envelope radius $\mathsf D^{-a}$ and depth $P=6K_{j+1}$. The formal condition requires the parent and central estimates of §5.1, a transported phase, the projected seed at every label, and the finite expansion satisfying its equations. It identifies $V=U_{j-1}+W^\natural$, its approximate Euler equation, $U_j=S_{\lambda_j^5}V$, and $O_j=(W-\langle W\rangle)^\natural$ on $[0,S_j]$. Fields are periodic lifts to $\mathbb R^3$; physical evaluation uses the inverse parent flow. The seed at the origin is identified with $\mathbf a_j$ on $[t_j,S_j]$. No corresponding identification of $\kappa_j$ with $(D_aX_{j-1})^{-T}k_*$ is recorded. This declaration specifies requirements for given step data; it does not prove their existence.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Steps: Fix a construction, a nonnegative integer envelope exponent $a$ and a Fourier cutoff symbol $\psi$. The formal condition asserts that, for every wave index $j\ge1$, there exist the phase, seed, time cutoff and finite expansion that realize step $j$ over $U_{j-1}$ on $[0,S_j]$. The expansion uses $\mathsf D=\lambda_{j-1}^9$, radius $\mathsf D^{-a}$ and depth $6K_{j+1}$; its physical evaluation produces $V$, $U_j=S_{\lambda_j^5}V$ and $O_j=W_{\rm osc}^\natural$. Thus one $a$ and one symbol serve all steps, while the profiles may vary with $j$. The central seed agrees with $\mathbf a_j$, but equality of the transported covector with $\kappa_j$ is not a required clause. The numbered theorem proves this condition for its constructed sequence.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.WaveOn: For paths $k,\mathbf a$ and a prescribed linear map $D(t)$ on a time set $J$, the formal condition is $k'=-D^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+2(k\cdot D\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ at every time in $J$. Derivatives are taken relative to $J$, allowing one-sided endpoint derivatives. This includes the first three relations of (2.1), but not its final condition $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$. Nonvanishing, zero trace, pressure compatibility and regularity of $D$ are also separate assumptions. Division by zero is assigned zero, so the equations are defined even for $k=0$; the nonzero physical-wave interpretation requires additional data.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.alpha: For the preceding wave’s orthonormal frame, set $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $\nu=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}$ and $S=\sigma/r$. At physical time $t=t_0+\tau/r$, the formal vector is $\alpha=(S E_1\cdot\mathbf a,E_2\cdot\mathbf a,S E_3\cdot\mathbf a)$. Thus $\mathbf a=\alpha_1E_1/S+\alpha_2E_2+\alpha_3E_3/S$, as in (2.3). Forming these coordinates does not impose the amplitude equation or transversality. The formula accepts every real $\tau$; the frame hypotheses and differential equations are guaranteed only where the physical time lies in the supplied compact set. Earlier intermediate formulas use the negative first component instead.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.corollary_8_3: Assume the common construction of Theorem 7.1, its smooth odd Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, and the formal Proposition 8.2 conclusions, including a uniform lower bound $c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ for central vorticity on every late activation interval. The theorem proves that $T_\infty>0$ is the maximal lifespan, that every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same data has that time, and that both integrals in (1.2) diverge. The norms are essential suprema over a unit cell, with the operator norm for $\nabla u$. The conclusion agrees with Corollary 8.3. Its formal proof uses the quantitative vorticity and crossing-time estimates; it does not prove the periodic Beale–Kato–Majda continuation criterion cited by the paper.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, and $\mathcal B(s)>0$ satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$. Suppose $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. The formal statement omits threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination from §1.5; the arithmetic result therefore applies under fewer assumptions.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_1: Let $J$ be a time interval on which relative derivatives are uniquely determined. Suppose $D$ is differentiable, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$, $D'+D^2$ is symmetric, and $k'=-D^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+p_{\rm w}k$, where $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$. Unlike the paper, the formal statement requires neither a smooth odd periodic profile nor its normalization; the Euler identity also allows $k=0$, using zero for division by zero. The interval derivative includes one-sided endpoint derivatives.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_2: Let nonzero perpendicular paths $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfy $k'=-B^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-B\mathbf a+2(k\cdot B\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ on a time set $J$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. Derivatives are assigned zero at points where they do not exist; regularity and the trajectory uniqueness hypotheses rule out that case in the application.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradient: For a velocity $U$ and two-time maps $X$, the formal definition is $M(t,a)=D_xU(t,X(0,t,a))$. The derivative is a linear map on Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$, with matrix entries $M_{ij}=\partial_jU_i$. For the smooth parent and its flow, this is the coefficient driving both $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and the Craik–Criminale seed equation in §3.1. The definition alone imposes no Euler equation, incompressibility or trajectory equation. At a spatial nondifferentiability point the formal derivative is assigned zero; the paper's smoothness assumptions ensure the usual gradient is used.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradientRate: For a parent velocity $u$ and particle flow $X$, set $M(t,a)=D_xu(t,X_{0,t}(a))$. This expression defines its time derivative with the label $a$ fixed, taken within $[0,T]$. At $t=0$ and $t=T$ it is the corresponding one-sided derivative. This is the $M_t$ in (4.1), not the derivative at fixed Eulerian position. If the derivative within the interval does not exist, the formal expression is assigned zero. This convention is irrelevant under the smooth-parent assumptions of §4 with $T>0$, which ensure the ordinary one-sided derivative at the endpoints and the usual derivative in the interior.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.meanHsharp: For $M(t,a)=D_xu(t,X_{0,t}(a))$, define $H^\#(t,a)=-(M_t(t,a)+M(t,a)^2)$, with time differentiation at fixed label within $[0,T]$. This is precisely the coefficient in (4.1). No symmetry is built into the definition. If $u$ solves Euler, (4.3) identifies it with the pressure Hessian along the flow; for a parent with residual $R$, the additional term is $-(\nabla R)\circ X$. The inverse requires the upper quadratic-form bound $H^\#\le I$, which is a separate assumption.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.meanKinetic: For a differentiable particle map $a\mapsto X_{0,t}(a)$, write $F=D_aX_{0,t}(a)$. The coefficient is $K=F^TF$, so $Kw\cdot w=|Fw|^2$. It is the kinetic matrix in (4.1), and the quadratic part of the label energy in (4.7). The transpose is the Euclidean adjoint and norms are operator norms. This definition gives nonnegativity, not a positive lower bound. If $F$ has inverse norm at most $D_->0$, the separate ellipticity estimate gives $K\ge D_-^{-2}I$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.meanVorticity: With $F=D_aX_{0,t}(a)$ and $M=D_xu(t,X_{0,t}(a))$, the coefficient is $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. It is the pulled-back vorticity in (4.1) and supplies the term $\Omega z_t\cdot z$ in the endpoint energy. The matrix convention is $(D_xu)_{ij}=\partial_ju_i$, fixing the sign of $M^T-M$. The formula does not require Euler or incompressibility. Its relation $K_t-\Omega=2F^TF_t$ uses the separately established flow identity $F_t=MF$.

notes.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_2: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. At sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|\bar f\|_{[n+1]}$ for every $n$. These are scaled label-derivative suprema on all of $[0,T]$. The exponent is chosen before the parent and order. This estimates existing solutions; it does not set $B(0)=0$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, the projected seed exists, and every depth $P\ge2$ admits a unique family of retained velocities and normalized pressures satisfying the mean and transverse recursions. The oscillations and their sources vanish before activation and outside the envelope; there the remainder is phase independent. Means need not vanish before activation. Smoothness is on the closed slab; no continuation across its endpoints is asserted.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1: For every common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, this theorem constructs smooth periodic velocity $u$ and mean-zero pressure $p$ solving Euler on $[0,T_\infty)$. The datum $u(0)$ is smooth, odd and divergence free, with $U_j(0)\to u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$. The velocity stays odd, and $U_j\to u$ uniformly in each such spatial norm on every $[0,S]$, $S<T_\infty$. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same data lasts at least to $T_\infty$ and agrees with $u$ there. This is a conditional comparison, not general maximal-solution existence; Corollary 8.3 later proves maximality of the constructed solution. The exact numerical Hölder norm is imported from a file not supplied here.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_2: For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, this theorem proves $\sup_{0\le t<T_\infty}\|u(t)\|_\infty<\infty$ and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$. In addition, fixed real $c>0,C$ give $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ for every sufficiently large $j$ and all $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$. Thus the blow-up is not restricted to a sequence of times. The spatial domain is the unit torus, represented by periodic fields on $\mathbb R^3$; the velocity norm is its essential supremum. The quantitative estimate is stronger than the printed Proposition 8.2 and is used with crossing lengths for the later integral argument.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_4: For the smooth periodic Euler limit of any common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, this theorem proves the two limits in Proposition 8.4. Given a compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and an integer $m\ge0$, $u(t)$ and $\partial_tu(t)$ converge uniformly on $K$ with every spatial derivative through order $m$, as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. The limits extend to $C^m$ fields near $K$. Removing the lattice means removing the torus origin, and the time derivative is taken inside $[0,T_\infty)$. The conclusion supplies spatial limits of the velocity and one time derivative; it does not require convergence of all higher time derivatives. The auxiliary note proves a stronger extension assertion for a suitably chosen construction.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAmplitude: For a real function $Y$ and time $\tau$, the formal expression is $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)=\exp(\int_0^\tau Y(s)\,ds)$, using the interval integral with its orientation when $\tau<0$. This defines a positive number for every input function. If the integral is not defined by an integrable function on the interval, the formal integral is assigned zero, giving amplitude one; this is not a claim of integrability. In the application, $Y$ solves (2.12) on $[0,\infty)$, hence is continuous there, and the ordinary integral gives the reference amplitude with $a_{\rm ref}(0)=1$ and $a_{\rm ref}'=Ya_{\rm ref}$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle: The formal angle is $\varphi(\tau)=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ for every real $\varepsilon,\tau$. It satisfies $\tan\varphi=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$, and for $\varepsilon\ge0$ lies in $[0,\pi/2)$. These specify the branch in (2.4); there is no ambiguity by integer multiples of $\pi$. The angle parametrizes the limiting direction $\tan\varphi E_1+E_3$ as the preceding shear tends to infinity. The definition does not claim that it is the actual angle of a finite-shear or perturbed wave, whose components must be estimated separately.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle_mem: For every $\varepsilon\ge0$ and every real $\tau$, the formal statement proves $0\le\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)<\pi/2$. This is the branch requirement for $\varphi$ in (2.4), extended to all real times. In particular the cosine is positive at every finite time. The result concerns the explicitly defined reference angle only; it does not constrain the actual wave vector of a finite-shear configuration. Neither an evolution equation nor the smallness condition (2.7) is a hypothesis.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.referenceSystemMatrix: Put $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. The formal matrix acting on $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ is $-\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$. Its second row therefore gives $\alpha_2'=-\alpha_1$, exactly as in (2.5). This definition uses the paper’s signs, unlike the intermediate matrix in coordinates $(-\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$. It is defined for all real parameters and times and is only a coefficient matrix: it neither constructs a solution nor proves that a particular amplitude satisfies the equation. Those assertions require separate differential-equation hypotheses or theorems.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2: There exist smooth odd divergence-free data $u_0$ on $\mathbb T^3$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, with $0<T_*<\infty$, bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and divergent time integrals of both gradient and vorticity norms. Velocity and its time derivative converge in every spatial $C^m$ norm on compact sets away from the origin. The velocity also extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from that point. Any maximal solution from $u_0$ has the same lifespan and velocity. The extension is periodic and need not solve Euler after $T_*$. This is the existential assertion of Remark 1.2, not an extension theorem for every singular solution.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.scaledNormSq: For a real scale $S$ and vector $\zeta\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal expression is $m=\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2$. When $S\ne0$ and $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$ in an orthonormal frame, it satisfies $|k|^2=\lambda^2m$. This is the factor after (2.3), not the ordinary Euclidean squared norm of $\zeta$. The definition also permits $S=0$: division by zero is assigned zero, so the middle term vanishes. To use $m$ as a nonzero pressure denominator, the amplitude equations impose positive $S$ and nonzero $\zeta_3$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix: For scale $S$, ratio $\varepsilon$ and scaled wave vector $\zeta$, put $m=\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2$ and $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/m$. At zero denominators the formal divisions are assigned zero, so existence of the matrix alone does not establish that this reduction is valid.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix_mulVe: Let $m=\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2$ and $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/m$. The formal statement proves that the finite-shear matrix applied to $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ has components $-\alpha_2+\zeta_1\Pi$ and $-(1-1/(2S^2))\alpha_1+\varepsilon(\zeta_1\alpha_1+\zeta_2\alpha_2)/(2S^2\zeta_3)+\zeta_2\Pi/S^2$. This verifies the algebra connecting the coefficient matrix to Lemma 2.3. The identity holds for arbitrary real inputs, including zero denominators because every division by zero is assigned zero. It is not an assertion that an amplitude solves this system; that requires the model wave hypotheses and $\zeta_3\ne0$.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearPressure: For $S,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ and $\zeta\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal formula is $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/(\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2)$. It is the pressure term in Lemma 2.3, linear in the two remaining amplitude components. The definition itself does not assume the model equations or positivity of the denominator. Division by zero is assigned zero; the lemma’s condition $\zeta_3\ne0$ ensures the ordinary pressure interpretation.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.tan_referenceAngle: For all real $\varepsilon,\tau$, the formal statement proves $\tan(\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2))=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$. This is the first relation in (2.4) with the explicitly chosen arctangent branch. It imposes no sign condition on $\varepsilon$ and involves no wave equation. The additional paper condition $0\le\varphi<\pi/2$ uses $\varepsilon\ge0$. Because arctangent always lies strictly between $-\pi/2$ and $\pi/2$, the tangent here does not encounter a pole at any finite real input.
notes.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_1_1: There exist smooth odd divergence-free periodic data $u_0$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$, with finite $T_*>0$. Velocity remains uniformly bounded, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and the time integrals of $\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty$ and $\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty$ both diverge. For every compact set away from the torus origin and every $m\ge0$, velocity and its time derivative converge in $C^m$. The formal statement further spells out the classical uniqueness implicit in the paper: every maximal solution from $u_0$ has endpoint $T_*$ and agrees with $u$ before it. Fields are periodic functions on $\mathbb R^3$; pressure has zero spatial mean.

Smooth force sources give smooth solutions of the linearized Euler equation and $b(0)=c$. Uniqueness concerns $z,v,c$ and the pressure gradient, on the specified interval. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.

The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. If $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, then at every order the transverse velocity, forcing and $\lambda$ times pressure have size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$; means and mean sources have size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2-2(p-2)/3}$; $C_{p+1}$ has size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-9/4-2(p-1)/3}$. notes.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: For each smooth radial Fourier cutoff and integer $a_0$, the theorem chooses $b\ge1$, an envelope exponent $a\ge a_0$ and fixed-order majorants. Every admissible threshold $\mathcal B$ above them permits construction for all sufficiently large $N$. Hölder bounds are pointwise in time, and the exact spatial norm definition is absent. The exponent can be chosen arbitrarily large; the assertion does not cover every sufficiently large exponent.

notes.TorusEuler.Paper.zetaRef: For real $\varepsilon,\tau$, the formal vector is $\zeta_0=(\tan\varphi,-\varepsilon\tau,1)=(\varepsilon\tau^2/2,-\varepsilon\tau,1)$, with $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. notes.TorusEuler.PaperAffine.exactWave: Let $J$ be a time interval on which relative derivatives are uniquely determined. notes.TorusEuler.PaperAffine.movingFrameDeriva: Let nonzero perpendicular paths $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfy $k'=-B^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-B\mathbf a+2(k\cdot B\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ on a time set $J$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$.
